description:
Hi everyone! We are a team of curious, creative, and passionate engineering students excited to take on the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

We are looking for enthusiastic people who enjoy challenges, teamwork, and thinking outside the box. You don't need to be an expert to join us; curiosity, creativity, and a willingness to learn are just as important.
summary:
Traveling with an Oaxaca Aeronautics is an educational video game where players build, and test rockets, spacecraft, and probes to complete missions from the Moon to other planets. Players start with a limited budget that determines which components they can use. They combine predefined parts (propulsion, tanks, modules, materials, instruments), each with its own cost, weight, and properties, and test their vehicle on a mission inspired by real NASA projects. If it fails, they analyze why, adjust the design, and try again.

Space exploration needs people who can solve problems under real constraints: limited budgets, mass limits, and risk of failure. Yet most students never experience this process, because rocket science feels distant and reserved for a few. By testing, and redesigning spacecraft, players learn that failure is part of engineering, and why every gram and every peso matters in a real mission. By connecting space exploration with Mexican culture, the game also shows young people in communities underrepresented in STEM that space is for them too, inspiring the next generation of Latin American explorers of missions like Artemis.
details:
Traveling with an Oaxacan is an educational video game where players design, build, and test rockets, spacecraft, and probes to complete missions across the Solar System, from the Moon to other planets. Players start with a limited budget and combine predefined parts (propulsion, tanks, modules, materials, and instruments), each with its own cost, weight, and properties. Then they test their vehicle on a mission inspired by real NASA projects. If the design fails, players analyze why, adjust it, and try again.

The game makes aerospace engineering accessible and fun. It teaches resource management, decision-making, and creative problem-solving, and it lets players recreate historical challenges and test different solutions. Because it uses real NASA data, players learn real science while playing.

Our intended impact is to bring more people, especially young people, closer to space science and help them understand how hard a real mission is. We want to turn the complexity of aerospace engineering into an interactive experience where imagination meets science.

We developed the project in Scratch, using block-based visual programming. Our data comes from official NASA websites covering the Apollo, Artemis, Gemini, and Mercury missions.

The project is creative because it turns players into engineers. Instead of just reading about missions, they build their own vehicles, manage a limited budget, and face the trade-offs of real mission designers. Every failure becomes a lesson and every redesign a new creative solution. The Oaxacan theme also gives the game a unique cultural identity.

Our team considered accessibility, using Scratch and predefined parts so beginners can play easily. We prioritized scientific accuracy through official NASA sources, and realism through budget, cost, and weight constraints. We also focused on educational value through a design, test, and redesign cycle, and on engagement, balancing fun and learning so players stay motivated.
